items.resumen: Eighty-eight years after pioneering British archaeologist Starkey was shot dead while traveling from the ancient city of Lachish to Jerusalem, researchers say they have uncovered compelling new evidence explaining who was behind his murder—and why he was targeted.

items.titulo: Researchers develop sensors for continuous corn growth monitoring
items.resumen: When is the best time to apply nitrogen? What plant response was there to fertilizer or any number of other treatments? There is a general answer to those questions now, but what if plant breeders and agronomists could download data from continuously monitored cornstalks and ears to develop specific answers for those questions?

items.titulo: How anxiety over climate change affects college students
items.resumen: College undergraduates are anxious about climate change, with many feeling powerless and frustrated about Earth's future, yet resources to help students cope are in short supply, according to new interdisciplinary University of Utah research. The sentiment isn't limited to students studying the environment.

items.titulo: A hidden star is plowing through Betelgeuse’s atmosphere, new evidence suggests
items.resumen: Something mysterious is disturbing Betelgeuse, and astronomers believe they have identified the culprit: a hidden companion star called Siwarha. New radio observations reveal that the smaller star may be plowing through Betelgeuse’s enormous atmosphere, creating disturbances that subtly stretch and distort the red supergiant’s shape.

items.titulo: One in 15 adults has experienced AI-generated image-based abuse, study finds
items.resumen: Around one in 15 adults has experienced AI-generated image-based abuse, according to a new study. items.resumen: A new study suggests that ultra-processed foods may influence children's developing brains in ways that encourage weight gain. items.titulo: Study maps Nelore cattle microbiota to reduce methane emissions
items.resumen: Researchers at the Brazilian Agricultural Research Corporation (EMBRAPA) are studying the relationship between the genetics of Nelore cattle and the microorganisms in their guts (microbiota). Nelore cattle are the most widely raised beef breed in Brazil. The goal is to develop strategies that reduce emissions of methane—a major greenhouse gas—and improve the animals' feed efficiency.

items.resumen_es: Científicos brasileños estudian la relación entre la genética del ganado Nelore y sus microorganismos intestinales. El objetivo es reducir las emisiones de metano y mejorar la eficiencia alimentaria.

items.titulo: North Atlantic's 'cold blob' may contain climate nuance
items.resumen: Climate observers have long tied the strength of a major ocean current to water temperatures in the so-called "cold blob" in the North Atlantic Ocean. The 965,000-square-mile (2.5 million square kilometers) area south and southeast of Greenland cooled by as much as 1.8 degrees Fahrenheit over the past century as other ocean waters warmed.

items.resumen_es: Aunque a menudo se piense lo contrario, la actividad humana en ciertos entornos naturales puede fomentar y nutrir de manera positiva la biodiversidad.

items.titulo: When humans disappear, biodiversity takes a surprising turn

items.titular_es: Cuando los humanos desaparecen, la biodiversidad toma un rumbo sorprendente
items.resumen_es: Mientras la conservación se ha centrado históricamente en los riesgos de la sobrepoblación, en ciertos lugares la despoblación humana es una amenaza real.

items.titulo: A healthier form of salt could prevent millions of deaths from stroke and heart disease
items.resumen: Switching from regular table salt to potassium-enriched salt could prevent millions of deaths worldwide each year, according to the first study on the potential global impact, published today in Nature Health.1

items.resumen_es: Cambiar la sal de mesa común por una enriquecida con potasio podría evitar millones de muertes anuales a nivel mundial por accidentes cerebrovasculares y cardiopatías.

items.titulo: Good sleep linked to better brain health in cardiometabolic disease
items.resumen: People with type 2 diabetes, heart disease or stroke who sleep well have better cognitive function and greater brain volume than people with the same conditions who sleep poorly, according to a new study from Karolinska Institutet. The researchers believe that good sleep may help to counteract the negative effects on the brain associated with these conditions.

items.resumen: An international team of researchers, led by scientists from the University of Plymouth (UK) and the Foundation for Biodiversity Research (France), has developed a framework which advocates for human harms from nature to be framed as avoidable risks that arise from the intersection of ecosystem hazards with human exposure and vulnerability. items.titulo: Enjoyment increases consumers’ willingness to pay for sustainable products
items.resumen: Consumers are more willing to pay for sustainable products if they also perceive them as enjoyable and appealing, according to a study conducted at the University of Eastern Finland. However, environmental friendliness alone does not always translate into willingness to pay.

items.resumen_es: Los consumidores están más dispuestos a pagar por productos sostenibles si además los perciben como atractivos y agradables, según un estudio de la Universidad de Finlandia Oriental.

items.titulo: Targeting multiple ageing-related processes with nutritional supplement shows promising effects on vascular health biomarkers
items.resumen: A multi-component nutritional supplement has been found to improve markers of vascular health, in a randomised controlled trial led by the University of Surrey. The formulation combined ingredients (vitamins/minerals, amino acids and plant-derived bio actives) selected for their relevance to several biological processes associated with ageing.

items.titulo: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
items.resumen: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. items.titulo: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?

items.titulo: Novo’s CEO still looking for deals to ‘close some of the gaps,’ as misfires hit profits
items.resumen: Novo’s CEO has told Fierce that the company remains on the hunt for deals that “close some of the gaps” in its pipeline, as the Big Pharma reports billions of dollars in impairment charges from a string of recent clinical misses.

items.titulo: AbbVie invests £120M in UK, including new R&D headquarters
items.resumen: AbbVie is investing 120 million pounds ($160 million) to expand its U.K. R&D presence, in a show of faith in the country’s life sciences sector.

items.titulo: Philips sets aside $322M for proposed DOJ settlement over sleep apnea device recall
items.resumen: Philips’ Respironics division has reached an “agreement in principle” with the U.S. Department of Justice to settle a long-running investigation into its recall of potentially defective sleep apnea devices.

items.titulo: Rhythm doubles down on LG obesity license, raising payout to as much as $855M
items.resumen: Rhythm Pharmaceuticals and LG Chem have rewritten the terms of their licensing agreement for the oral obesity and hyperphagia drug bivamelagon, growing to $855 million in scheduled payments from the earlier milestone-based deal of $305 million.

items.titulo: AbbVie abandons phase 2 solid tumor drug over ‘limited benefit’
items.resumen: AbbVie has scrapped a phase 2 solid tumor drug after deciding that the monoclonal antibody was unlikely to best the current standard of care, Fierce has learned.

items.titulo: Pfizer pares back obesity pipeline, drops phase 2-stage lung disease candidate
items.resumen: Pfizer has axed a phase 2 pulmonary arterial hypertension program on business grounds, dealing a setback to a long-running effort to treat the lung disease by targeting BMP9.

items.titulo: Abbott's Tectonic test looks to shift artery disease treatment with ‘early’ win
items.resumen: Abbott has posted positive 30-day results from its Tectonic trial of the investigational SonicForce Coronary IVL System in coronary artery disease (CAD), but analysts urge caution on results.

items.titulo: BioArctic left out in the cold as Novartis walks away from $800M neuro collab
items.resumen: Just 14 months after Novartis signed an $800 million biobucks neuroscience partnership with BioArctic, the Swiss pharma has walked away from the deal.

items.titulo: FDA grants uniQure’s Huntington’s gene therapy priority review, teeing up ‘defining milestone’
items.resumen: The FDA has accepted uniQure’s priority review and application for its gene therapy treatment for Huntington’s disease.

items.titulo: Karyopharm files Chapter 11, lines up Ayrmid as lead bidder in planned merger
items.resumen: In an answer to Karyopharm's cash crisis, Irish biotech Ayrmid has agreed to make the first bid on the struggling biopharma's assets in a court supervised auction, teeing up a potential hematology merger.

items.titulo: OpenAI-funded Biossil snags Theriva's unwanted antibiotic degrader portfolio for up to $91M
items.resumen: Canada's OpenAI-backed startup Biossil Labs has extended its pharma shopping spree with a deal worth up to $91 million for Theriva Biologics' deprioritized early- to mid-stage portfolio of antibiotic-degrading enzymes.

items.titulo: Teva ends trial of one of its original line-up of innovative meds over futility
items.resumen: Teva has given up on a key trial of one of its original line-up of innovative medicines.

items.titulo: FDA dims Bright Minds’ outlook with partial hold on seizure trial over toxicity in mice
items.resumen: The FDA has put a partial hold on Bright Minds Biosciences’ seizure study application over preclinical toxicity data and concerns about its preparations for enrolling children.

items.titulo: Lower dose of Tiziana's MS drug reduces neuroinflammation, while higher dose struggles
items.resumen: Tiziana Life Sciences’ intranasal drug has hit the dual endpoints of a phase 2a study in patients with a form of multiple sclerosis (MS), although the win was slightly marred by the higher dose missing a key neuroinflammation goal.

items.titulo: Madrigal’s Rezdiffra storms past blockbuster milestone as CEO hails ‘accelerating’ MASH market
items.resumen: To Madrigal CEO Bill Sibold, “it’s hard to find a more attractive growth opportunity in biotech” than MASH, as the company’s Rezdiffra, the first FDA-approved MASH therapy, crossed the $1 billion mark in annual sales.

items.titulo: Amgen's quality chief to retire as internal successor steps up
items.resumen: Jackie Elbonne, Ph.D., announced her retirement after 35 years in the biopharma industry, leaving Amgen's chief quality officer role to her deputy, Aine Hanly, Ph.D.

items.titulo: Pfizer delivers Q3 beat as post-COVID comeback gains momentum
items.resumen: Pfizer's third-quarter performance bested Wall Street estimates thanks to an Eliquis beat and 37% growth from acquired products.

items.titulo: As Bayer spots pharma recovery, questions resurface over potential crop science split
items.resumen: Bayer’s pharmaceutical business may finally be entering a long-awaited growth cycle, but CEO Bill Anderson still can’t quite escape the lingering questions around a potential crop science split.

items.titulo: Lonza bets big on US growth, snaps up Merck KGaA’s CDMO business
items.resumen: Lonza will purchase the German Merck’s U.S.-based CDMO network for mid-triple-digit million euros. Besides five sites, the deal will bolster Lonza’s prowess in rapidly growing sectors such as cell and gene therapy, bioconjugates, viral vectors and advanced drug-delivery technologies.

items.titulo: Sumitomo's Gemtesa power couple takes the wheel in road-trip themed overactive bladder awareness push

items.titulo: Hansoh hit with FDA write-up after inspection

items.titulo: Inovio’s DNA-based immunotherapy Voceryq approved by FDA for rare HPV airway disease
items.resumen: After an initial FDA scare that threatened its path for an accelerated approval, Inovio’s Voceryq, the first plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy, has earned a go-ahead to treat a rare HPV-driven disease.
